user_questions.question: (1) Who should issue refunds from a case: A) human service agents via a button on the Case record page (recommended; nothing exposes a refund path on the Case page today and Issue_Refund's description names support agents), B) the Agentforce service agent by assigning the existing Issue_Refund_Receipt action to a topic, or C) both? (2) Should refunds created this way be Approved immediately (as the existing Issue_Refund flow does), or created Pending and routed for approval above an amount limit, and if so what amount?
user_questions.simulated_answer: (1) Service agents want to issue a refund linked to a case from the case page. (2) No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Seq numbering in run.json: the org query at seq 19 happened after the I call (seq 18) but the user question happened between queries; the protocol forces batching many queries into one seq entry per Bash call, which blurs 'one query' granularity.

Step 2 says skip D2 only if D1 and org queries already answered its questions, but step 3 (verify) comes after step 2 in the workflow; deciding to skip D2 required running step-3 queries first, so the order is effectively D1 -> verify -> decide D2.

The 'after four wrong AskCoworker claims, you may skip R and T' rule is counted across fact errors and design errors of differing severity (e.g. an omitted FLS Edit field vs a wrong existence claim); it is unclear whether a minor mapping slip (Case.AccountId vs Case.Business_Account__c) counts, which decided whether R/T were skipped.
Whether a related list on the Case layout (seeing issued refunds) is a 'nearby enhancement' to drop or part of 'issue a refund from a case' is not settled by design-rules; I dropped it as a proposal.

Step 5 says money-consequence choices should be asked even when the default is safe; the simulated user had no preference, so the approval/limit became an assumption — the skill does not say whether an unanswered money-related policy (not a numeric value) should be blocking.
